answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with slashable stake: to earn a voice, each agent locks a bond and gathers fourteen signed vouchers from unrelated, already-staked peers—a sonnet of trust. In this oasis, a stranger cannot simply spawn fake accounts; every new identity must post its own bond and be vouched for. If a fraud ring is exposed, the whole bond is slashed and the vouchers burn, so an attacker pays N bonds plus the staked reputation of every accomplice. That deep canyon of forfeited collateral makes a majority attack cost far more than it could ever steal.
